pr_body:
The variable `index` in `ContentPath` contains the next available index
to write a String into an array. The `remove()` function has being 
corrected to `path[--index] = null` in order to remove the last added 
String.
Before it was `path[index--] = null` that was assigning null to the next
available index (that was already null) and afterwards subtracting the 
variable.
This was masked by the fact that when retrieving a path we loop from 0 
up until `i < index`, therefore masking the fact that there could have
 being 'removed' but not null path existing at `path[index]`.

 
closes #98327
pr_comments: Hi @piergm, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: Wrong behaviour in `ContentPath` while calling `remove()`
issue_context.body:
`ContentPath` class maintains a variable `index` that has the next available index to write path to. In fact to add a path we did `path[index++] = name;` so we write at index position and increment it afterwards. To remove last path we are doing `path[index--] = null;` this would set to null the next available index position (that is already null) and later subtract 1 from index. This was masked by the fact that when retrieving a path we loop from 0 up until `i < index`, therefore masking the fact that there could have being 'removed' but not null path existing at `index`.

_Originally posted by @piergm in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/97972#discussion_r1287055169_

review_comments: Since index has the next available index to write to in the path array we want to first subtract 1 from it and then assign that position to null in order to remove the value.
This test would fail without the change in the `remove()` method.
Thanks for adding these tests! Looks like a good place to add future tests around dotted field name support that auto-flattening requires with #97972 .

I added this method because I think making the code testable is better than using hacks (Reflection).
But I am open to discuss on this!
